body:
## Parent and context
Parent program: #5678. Product/implementation foundation: #2048. This ticket owns the evidence-backed competitor feature inventory and matrix that the cluster designs can use; it does not implement features or silently settle the program-level open questions.

## Scope
- Define a repeatable enumeration method and a normalized feature vocabulary for Obsidian, Evernote, Notion, OneNote, NotebookLM, Logseq, Joplin, Anytype, and Open Knowledge (whose identity is not yet confirmed).
- Record each product’s data model, sync, sharing/permissions, pricing or lock-in where it affects import/export, and distinguishing capabilities.
- Compare features in a product-by-feature matrix with qualitative notes about depth/quality and meaningful implementation differences; avoid checkbox-only conclusions.
- Use primary documentation and, where authorized and feasible, hands-on evaluation. Record product edition/version, source and observation dates, evidence type, uncertainty, unavailable evidence, and gaps.
- Trace candidate clusters to the existing follow-ons #5837–#5844 and identify any matrix-driven additions or changes. For each candidate, record evidence and adopt/adapt/reject options without treating competitor presence as a default requirement.

## Required outputs
1. A short method and source/provenance note, including how product editions and feature names are normalized.
2. A linked matrix document with product inventories, comparative notes, and evidence links.
3. A findings section connecting observations to the existing cluster designs and recording unresolved decisions rather than deciding them by assumption.

## Read-authority constraint (already ruled; do not re-litigate)
The knowledge layer defaults to public read; owners may grant reads to any number of groups and/or users. Resolution order is **object → user default → server config → public**. Any inventory or recommendation involving sharing, search, graph visibility, or AI-over-notes must describe compatibility with this rule and must not suggest a read path that exposes content the resolved policy denies.

## Open Drew-owned program questions — still open, not assumptions
Carry these questions into the investigation and record whether each affects the matrix or requires an explicit decision; do not answer them by guessing: product versions/editions (free vs. paid); hands-on evaluation vs. documentation-only budget per product; the identity of “Open Knowledge”; graph scope (all ID objects vs. knowledge-only in v1); and AI-over-notes model choice (local, hosted, or user choice) and its read-authority implications.

## Acceptance criteria
- The method, normalized product/feature inventories, and matrix document are complete, sourced, and linked from #5678.
- Every in-scope product is covered or has an explicit evidence/identity blocker; matrix entries distinguish confirmed facts from unknowns.
- Cluster findings link to the existing tickets and state evidence-backed options without silently adopting features or resolving Drew-owned questions.
- Read-authority compliance is explicit, including visibility-sensitive AI/search/graph findings.
